records.question: Why did capital expenditure rise in 2025?
records.expected_answer: Larger projects: the Pennine theatre complex, the emergency department rebuild at St Wystan's and the MRI replacement at Alderbank

answer.answer: Capital expenditure rose to 96.4 million pounds (from 71.0 million in 2024) largely because spending had been held back during the pandemic and had been increasing since 2022; in 2025 the largest projects were the new theatre complex at Pennine Orthopaedic Centre (opened on schedule in the autumn), the rebuilding of the emergency department at St Wystan's Hospital, and the replacement of MRI scanners at Alderbank General Hospital. Money saved from lower agency staffing costs was also used to open additional beds and extend evening clinics.

citations.quote: Capital expenditure reached 96.4 million pounds, up from 71.0 million pounds in 2024. The largest projects were the new theatre complex
The money saved was used to open additional beds and to extend evening clinics.

answer.judge_reason: The answer identifies the same three major projects (Pennine theatre complex, St Wystan's emergency department rebuild, Alderbank MRI replacement) as the cause, plus additional correct detail.
